prize_parts.citation: for the development of base editing, the programmable chemical conversion of single DNA bases without double-strand cleavage
for the invention of targeted protein degradation by heterobifunctional molecules that induce proximity to the ubiquitin ligase machinery

statement.case_for: I keep my round-1 configuration after reading the full exchange, and I tested it against the chair's own questions. Targeted protein degradation is the only candidacy that all eight members ranked and that four place in a preferred configuration; its principle (event-driven, catalytic removal by induced proximity, with quantifiable ternary-complex cooperativity) is new and has no earlier prize. Base editing is a defined chemical reaction, deamination of a displaced strand, that produces single-nucleotide change without a double-strand break; it differs mechanistically from the Cas9 cleavage recognised in 2020, has been reproduced independently, and is already used in patients. On the chemistry question put to us, the cytosine editor is the repurposing of an APOBEC-type deaminase on single-stranded DNA, and the adenine editor required evolving TadA, an RNA enzyme, to act on DNA, which has no natural counterpart. Both are one concept, and Liu conceived and directed it. Pairing the two keeps the prize within three people and gives supporters of either one a vote for a configuration they already named.
statement.case_against: Base editing sits close to the 2020 prize, the field is about ten years old, and a Liu-only citation leaves out Komor and Gaudelli, who carried out the key experiments, and Kondo and Nishida, who reported parallel deaminase editing. Degraders have no approved PROTAC drug yet to my knowledge, and a Crews and Deshaies citation omits Ciulli and the cereblon glue strand of Handa, Ito and Gray, which may be the more clinically advanced discovery. A two-part prize from chemical biology also leaves out core chemistry with cleaner attribution, B008 and B037, and no candidacy has five explicit supporters on the round-1 files.

responses.point: Aili proposes Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli for degradation, arguing that Ciulli's structure-based VHL ligands and ternary-complex rules made the concept drug-like, while accepting that the cereblon glue strand cannot be fitted into three names.
responses.response: I take the Ciulli argument seriously and have not dismissed it. My criterion for choosing between Ciulli and Handa for a third place is the one the chair asked for: who first showed the principle, not who made it tractable. On that test Crews and Deshaies hold the concept and first demonstrations, Ciulli's work is the design refinement that followed, and Handa's discovery of cereblon as the thalidomide target is a separate finding about molecular glues that a PROTAC citation should not appear to claim. I therefore keep two names, which is also what allows Liu to stay in the prize. If the committee prefers Aili's three names for degradation alone, I would see that as a coherent single-part prize, but I would then lose the base-editing part and I do not think that trade is better.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks degradation first but asks whether mechanism confirmation without an approved PROTAC drug justifies recognition now, and he lists base editing only as an alternative because of the 2020 prize.
responses.response: His maturity question is the right one, and I would answer it by limiting the citation, as I have, to the mechanism and design principle (induced proximity with ubiquitin ligases), not to a therapeutic outcome. Many laboratories have reproduced that principle and degraders are in human trials, which is a stronger record than we required for other chemistry prizes where the use followed the award. On base editing and 2020, I do not agree that proximity in time makes it a refinement: the 2020 reaction is DNA cleavage and repair, while a base editor catalyses a chemical conversion of one base to another. I ask him whether a citation that names the deamination chemistry explicitly would meet his concern.

responses.point: Somfai pairs Buchwald and Hartwig (B008) with Liu alone for base editing, stresses the lack of any maturity concern for C-N coupling, and argues the 2010 prize covered C-C coupling only.
responses.response: We now agree on Liu alone for base editing, and I accept his argument that the 2010 prize does not cover amination and that the ligand-controlled catalytic method is the achievement, not Kosugi's stoichiometric tin chemistry. That makes B008 the strongest alternative to my second part, and I would support it as a stand-alone prize if base editing and degradation fail to reach a majority. I keep degradation in my configuration because I weigh the capability it opened more than the long record of B008, but I recognise that this is a judgment about generative potential and not a scientific defect in his candidate. I would like to know whether he would vote for B061 with B028 if B008 cannot get five.

responses.point: Chabes places base editing alone as the prize, proposing Liu, Komor and Gaudelli, since the cytosine and adenine editors are separate chemical achievements, and notes Kondo and Nishida as an unavoidable gap.
responses.response: I agree that the two editors are chemically separate, and his point about evolving TadA is the strongest argument for crediting Gaudelli. I still prefer a Liu-only citation, because both editors are products of one programme under one concept, and adding Komor and Gaudelli forces the committee to adjudicate Kondo and Nishida's parallel Target-AID work, which in a three-name limit is best avoided by a citation to the method and its originator. I also cannot support base editing as a stand-alone prize when its closeness to 2020 is the main objection raised by three colleagues, which is why I pair it with an achievement that has no prior prize.

responses.point: Zou proposes Buchwald and Hartwig as the whole prize and argues that C-N reductive elimination required a distinct solution, making this more than an extension of the 2010 prize.
responses.response: I accept that argument and I accept that the maturity and attribution here are the cleanest on the shortlist. My disagreement is only that for a broad audience it delivers fewer unforeseen opportunities than the other two parts, which is a weaker ground than the objections to B061 and B028. I have kept it as my first alternative and would vote for it should the pairing fail.

uncertainties: Whether five members can be found for any single configuration, given that the opening ranks of B028 and B061 are split.
Whether a Liu-only citation can be defended against Komor and Gaudelli, and whether Kondo and Nishida's Target-AID priority is comparable.

Whether limiting a degrader citation to Crews and Deshaies without Ciulli or the cereblon strand is acceptable, and whether degrader clinical validation is sufficient; I rely on general knowledge, not current trial data.
Whether a two-part chemical-biology prize is the right balance against core chemistry such as B008.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any shortlisted candidate: none is at Lund, in NanoLund, or a known collaborator. Somfai and Sparr are Lund colleagues, which is not a conflict with any candidate; no recusal is needed.
